purpose: Establish whether a lean workflow/Agent child whose agent definition declares a skill in frontmatter receives that skill in its initial context (listing and full SKILL.md body) without reading it from disk, against a child whose definition declares no skill.
preregistered: Written before dispatch: if the declared child quotes the SKILL.md first heading and a distinctive body sentence verbatim with zero tool uses, and the control child reports no skill, worker-level preloading of declared skills is established on this host and Claude Code version; if the declared child reports only a name/description or nothing, it is refuted for this configuration.

commands.output_excerpt: body_present=true; body_first_heading='# Build with TypeSafe'; body_sentence='Code owns the workflow; the model supplies programmable common sense where ordinary code needs semantic understanding.'; mechanism: body injected at start with 'Base directory for this skill: ~/.claude/skills/typesafe-ai'; tool_uses=0

commands.cmd: Agent(subagent_type=source-scout, same probe, control: no skills declared)
commands.output_excerpt: typesafe_listed=false; body_present=false; no skill mechanism in context; tool_uses=0

16:# Build with TypeSafe; 23-24: 'Code owns the workflow; the model / supplies programmable common sense where ordinary code needs semantic understanding.' (quotes match verbatim across the line break)

commands.cmd: python3 scan of the two children's native session transcripts (Claude Code subagent JSONL): count tool_use blocks; find messages containing the skill command marker and the SKILL.md body; compare the whitespace-normalized body (frontmatter stripped) with the injected text
commands.output_excerpt: declared: 13 records, 0 tool_use blocks, 2 messages carrying <command-name>typesafe-ai</command-name>, full SKILL.md body (9,301 chars, whitespace-normalized) contained in the injected message; control: 12 records, 0 tool_use blocks, no skill marker, no body

result: Settled from the native session transcripts, not only from the children's self-reports (Codex review of PR #111 asked for this). The declared child's transcript (agent definition declares skills: [typesafe-ai]) contains, before any tool use, a message carrying the typesafe-ai skill marker with the complete SKILL.md body (whitespace-normalized body of 9,301 characters, frontmatter stripped, fully contained), and the child made 0 tool calls. The control child's transcript (no declared skill) has no skill marker and no body. The declared child also quoted the heading and a body sentence that match the installed file verbatim. So a lean child whose definition declares a skill gets the full skill body preloaded; the loaded copy is the user-installed one, currently byte-identical to the project copy.

verdict_impact.explanation: Confirms the incumbent practice (declare skills per agent in frontmatter) delivers the skill body to workers; it also shows the user-installed copy, not the project copy, is what loads, which matters for version pinning.

limitations: Self-reported context introspection by the child models: the quoted text is checkable against the file (it matches), but the mechanism description is the model's reading of its own context.
One declared/control pair on Claude Code 2.1.280; Codex workers are not covered.

The loaded copy is the user-installed skill. At probe time it is byte-identical to the project copy (.agents/skills/typesafe-ai/SKILL.md, sha256 71ea90d7…), so no drift; if they diverge, the worker gets the user copy.

The control differs from the declared arm in more than the skills declaration (agent type source-scout vs semantic-evidence-reviewer, model, omitClaudeMd), so the transcripts show the declared child received the body, but the control does not isolate the declaration as the only difference.
